Issuing Authority: Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB), Bundesallee 100, 38116 Braunschweig, Germany. Person responsible: Dr. Gudrun Wendt.

Applicant: Elster Water Metering Limited, 130 Camford Way, Sundon Park, Luton, Bedfordshire, LU3 3AN, United Kingdom.

"Manufacturer of the certified type is the applicant and" — additional manufacturers:
- Elster Metering LTD (Circle Ring Network), No. 10 Jalan Jurutera U1/23, Section U1, Kawasan Perindustrial Hicom Glenmarie, 40150 Shah Alam, Selangor Darul Ehsan, Malaysia
- Elster Water Metering s.r.o., 8. apríla 259, 91601 Stará Turá, Slovenská republika

Certified type: Water meter intended for the metering of cold potable water
Type: Q200 Q3=1.6 (E, P, M), Q200 Q3=2.5 (E, P, M), SM250 (E, P, M), SM700 (E, P, M)

Category: "Water meter" — schema example categories listed: "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system", "Fuel dispenser", "Taximeter", "Gas meter", ... Water meter is fine.

Date issued: 17.07.2014 → 2014-07-17.

Recommendation: R49 (OIML R49), parts 49-1, 49-2, 49-3, edition 2006. Accuracy class 2 (from metrology table). Scheme: The certificate says scheme... OIML-CS certificates have scheme A or B. This cert (2006) — actually pre-dates OIML-CS. The recommendation block includes scheme field. Not mentioned in the document; I could omit scheme or set null. Rule 8: don't fabricate. I'll omit scheme.

project_number: R3-0033 appears on page 1 ("R3-0033"). That's the project number. Actually "R3-0033" might be a PTB reference. I'll include as project_number.

page_total: 3 ("Page 1 of 3 pages").

member_state: Germany.

oiml_issuer_id: not mentioned explicitly. PTB's OIML issuer ID... not present in markdown. Omit.

Test reports:
- PTB-1.5-4036396, Revision 5 (94 pages) — Report No.
- PTB-1.5-4025664, Revision 7 (95 pages) — Test Report No.

Roles: first is "Report" — role: type_evaluation_report perhaps. The text: "results of tests and examinations provided in the associated Report No. PTB-1.5-4036396, Revision 5 (94 pages) and Test Report No. PTB-1.5-4025664, Revision 7 (95 pages)." So report id PTB-1.5-4036396, revision 5, pages 94, role type_evaluation_report. Test report PTB-1.5-4025664, revision 7, pages 95, role test_report.

No dates for reports.

revision_history: The certificate is Revision 8 but no revision history details given. Revision 8 is part of the certificate number context. Should I include revision_history with revision "8"? The schema's revision_history is changes list; we don't know changes. Hmm. The certificate number itself includes "Revision 8". I could omit revision_history since no changes known. But maybe include? Rule: don't fabricate. Omit.

Now the metrology characteristics tables.

Models:
- Q200 Q3=1.6 (E, P, M) — table 2: Q3=1.6 m³/h, Q4=2.0, Q2/Q1=1.6, Q1 ∈ {0.010, 0.008, 0.0064}, Q2 ∈ {0.016, 0.0128, 0.01024}, Q3/Q1 ∈ {160, 200, 250}, length 110 mm, thread G ¾" B.
- Q200 Q3=2.5 (E, P, M) — table 1 first column group (colspan 3): Q3=2.5, Q4=3.125, Q2/Q1=1.6, Q1 ∈ {0.0156, 0.0125, 0.010}, Q2 ∈ {0.025, 0.020, 0.016}, Q3/Q1 ∈ {160, 200, 250}, length 110 mm, thread G ¾" B.
- SM250 (E,P) — Q3=4.0, Q4=5.0, Q2/Q1=1.6, Q1 ∈ {0.020, 0.025}, Q2 ∈ {0.032, 0.040}, Q3/Q1 ∈ {200, 160}, length 190 mm, thread G 1" B.
- SM700 (E,P) — Q3=4.0, Q4=5.0, Q2/Q1=1.6, Q1 ∈ {0.020, 0.025}, Q2 ∈ {0.032, 0.040}, Q3/Q1 ∈ {200, 160}, length 190 mm, thread 1" or 1¼" NPSM.

Interesting: Q1 and Q2 vary with Q3/Q1 ratio (the ratio designation). Within each model there are variants by Q3/Q1 ratio: 160, 200, 250. So each model has multiple Q1/Q2 depending on ratio. This is a config axis: ratio Q3/Q1.

The model designations: Q200 Q3=1.6 and Q200 Q3=2.5 themselves encode Q3. And each has (E, P, M) variants — likely E, P, M denote different installation orientations (E = horizontal, P = vertical, M = ...?). Actually for Elster V100/Q200: E = horizontal pipe, P = vertical pipe upward, M = mixed? These are installation position variants.

So there are sub-variants per model by Q3/Q1 ratio: 160/200/250 for Q200 models, and 200/160 for SM250/SM700.

How to model this? Options:
1. model_family with 4 models (Q200 Q3=1.6, Q200 Q3=2.5, SM250, SM700), and config_level entries for q1/q2/q3_ratio with axis "Q3/Q1 ratio".

For q1 varying within a model by ratio, we can do config_level:
- attribute: q1, unit m³/h, axis: "Q3/Q1 ratio", values: [{condition: "Q200 Q3=1.6, Q3/Q1=160", value: 0.010}, ...]

Or create model-level entries with model_id including the ratio, e.g., "Q200 Q3=1.6 (Q3/Q1=160)". Hmm. The R137 example put size variants as models. Here the type list is explicit: 4 types. The ratios are sub-variants. I think using config_level with axis = "Q3/Q1 ratio" and conditions combining model + ratio is cleanest.

Alternatively, expand models to 10 variants: Q200 Q3=1.6 has 3 ratios, Q200 Q3=2.5 has 3, SM250 has 2, SM700 has 2 → 10 variants. Then model_level matrix fully covers q1, q2, q3, q4 etc. q3, q4 constant per model but repeated per ratio variant. That's also acceptable per "Models[]: one entry per variant".

I think the more faithful approach: model_family with the 4 named types; config_level for ratio-dependent attributes (q1, q2, q3_over_q1 itself, and q3_over_q1 ratio attribute at model level with list... hmm q3/q1 has multiple values per model).

Let me use config_level:
- attribute "q1", unit "m³/h", axis "model and Q3/Q1 ratio": conditions like "Q200 Q3=1.6, ratio 160" → 0.010 etc.
- attribute "q2", unit "m³/h", axis same.
- attribute "q3_over_q1", axis same: 160/200/250 values dimensionless.

And model_level for attributes constant per model: q3, q4, q2_over_q1, length, thread.

Actually, thread varies per model: G ¾" B, G 1" B, 1" or 1¼" NPSM. String values.

Alternatively expand the models to include ratio variants to make the matrix cleaner. The R137 example did that (size G1.6 vs G2.5 as models). Here the type designations are explicitly given as 4 types; the ratio is an internal variant. I'll go with config_level.

Hmm, but maybe simpler and more complete: define models as 10 variants with model_id like "Q200 Q3=1.6 / Q3/Q1=160". Then model_level entries for q3, q4, q2_over_q1, q1, q2, q3_over_q1, length, thread. That duplicates q3 etc. across ratio variants. It's verbose but complete and machine-friendly. The rules say models[] one entry per variant. The ratio variants are genuine variants (different Q1). I'll do this: models list with 10 entries.

Wait, but the (E, P, M) suffixes: Q200 Q3=1.6 (E, P, M) means the type covers three installation positions E, P, M. SM250 (E, P, M) per the type list, but the metrology table says "SM250 (E,P)". The type identification says all four types have (E, P, M). The table headers show SM250 (E,P) and SM700 (E,P). Slight discrepancy; I'll keep the type designations as listed: "Q200 Q3=1.6 (E, P, M)", "Q200 Q3=2.5 (E, P, M)", "SM250 (E, P, M)", "SM700 (E, P, M)".

Attributes per model (constant within model):
- q3: 1.6 / 2.5 / 4.0 / 4.0 m³/h
- q4: 2.0 / 3.125 / 5.0 / 5.0 m³/h
- q2_over_q1: 1.6 all
- length: 110 / 110 / 190 / 190 mm
- thread: "G ¾\" B" / "G ¾\" B" / "G 1\" B" / "1\" or 1¼\" NPSM"

Ratio-dependent:
Q200 Q3=1.6: ratio 160 → Q1 0.010, Q2 0.016; ratio 200 → Q1 0.008, Q2 0.0128; ratio 250 → Q1 0.0064, Q2 0.01024.
Q200 Q3=2.5: ratio 160 → Q1 0.0156, Q2 0.025; ratio 200 → Q1 0.0125, Q2 0.020; ratio 250 → Q1 0.010, Q2 0.016.
SM250: ratio 200 → Q1 0.020, Q2 0.032; ratio 160 → Q1 0.025, Q2 0.040.
SM700: ratio 200 → Q1 0.020, Q2 0.032; ratio 160 → Q1 0.025, Q2 0.040.

Verify: Q3/Q1 for SM250 with Q3=4.0, Q1=0.020 → 200 ✓; Q1=0.025 → 160 ✓. Q2/Q1 = 1.6: 0.032/0.020=1.6 ✓; 0.040/0.025=1.6 ✓.

Q200 Q3=2.5: Q1=0.0156 → 2.5/0.0156 = 160.3 ≈ 160 ✓; 0.0125 → 200 ✓; 0.010 → 250 ✓. Q2 = 1.6×Q1: 0.02496 ≈ 0.025, 0.020, 0.016 ✓.

Q200 Q3=1.6: 1.6/0.010=160 ✓; 1.6/0.008=200 ✓; 1.6/0.0064=250 ✓. Q2: 0.016, 0.0128, 0.01024 ✓.

Table order in the first table for Q200 Q3=2.5: Q1 columns 0.0156, 0.0125, 0.010 correspond to Q3/Q1 160, 200, 250. Yes aligned.

SM250: Q1 0.020, 0.025 correspond to Q3/Q1 200, 160. Yes aligned as given.

So 10 model variants if expanded. Let me decide: I'll expand to 10 variants since the matrix detection rule emphasizes capturing variant coverage. Model IDs:

I'll include a matrix_tables entry "Metrology characteristics by model" with columns model, q3, q4, q2_over_q1, q1, q2, q3_over_q1, length, thread. With 10 rows. That's redundant but per instructions "preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere" — here it fits elsewhere, so maybe optional. The R137 example included both. I'll include the matrix table for fidelity. Actually the schema says matrix_tables is for tables that don't fit elsewhere; but the example R137 extracted it into matrix_tables AND model_level. I'll follow that pattern with one matrix table.

Hmm, it's a judgment call. To be safe and information-complete, include matrix_tables with the two tables merged or two separate tables. I'll do two separate matrix_tables entries matching the two tables, plus the common characteristics table type-level.
